item.title: 2025_PBM_1: Update the Patient blood management guideline for adults with critical bleeding and associated specialist services
item.description:
The National Blood Authority is seeking responses from potential suppliers to:

  1. update the Patient blood management guideline for adults with critical bleeding (the Guideline), trialling a living guideline approach. The purpose of the updated Guideline is to provide evidence-based recommendations, reflecting current evidence and best practice.
  2. as required, assist with the development of a variety of stakeholder communication and engagement materials.
  3. upon request, the Potential Supplier is to evaluate the evidence base across Patient Blood Management Guidelines: Module 2 Perioperative, Module 3 Medical, Module 4 Critical Care, Module 5 Obstetrics and Maternity, and Module 6 Neonatal and Paediatrics; and the Guideline for the prophylactic use of Rh D immunoglobulin in pregnancy care.

The updated Guideline will need to be developed in accordance with the National Health and Medical Research Council’s (NHMRC) Guidelines for Guidelines Handbook to meet NHMRC Standards, currently the 2016 NHMRC Standards for Guidelines available at www.nhmrc.gov.au/guidelinesforguidelines/standards. The Guideline must be capable of being approved by the NHMRC.

Building on the successful establishment of the Grain Automate Hub and earlier extension activities, this investment will deliver the next phase of the Grain Automate Extension Program to expand national reach, strengthen regionally relevant delivery and provide growers with practical learning pathways for adoption of these technologies. Through nationally coordinated workshops, demonstrations, digital learning resources and readiness tools, the program will enhance grower capability, support informed investment decisions, and accelerate the adoption of automation-enabled farming systems that improve productivity, labour efficiency and whole-farm performance.

item.title: PROC-9177419: Building out the Nitrogen Mission
item.description:
Australian grain growers are among the most innovative in the world but need a breakthrough in nitrogen (N) management. GRDC has been investing in new frontiers in nitrogen management for many years and is well positioned to scale up that investment in a structured, long-term, and strategic manner via the building out of the Nitrogen Mission. The recent fertiliser supply crisis exemplifies the need to do so. Specifically, GRDC has ambitions to decrease long-term (historical) N costs as a percentage of crop revenue by 50% or more, halve current N losses to the environment, and decrease emissions intensity associated with N usage by at least 20%. In the process GRDC aims to build out world-leading research capacity and science and technology innovation in N management in the Australian grains industry. The opportunity for partners is to coinvest with GRDC in delivering a breakthrough that unlocks major economic, social, and environmental benefits in the Australian grains industry, and potentially, other agricultural markets internationally. Even a 15% reduction in long-term nitrogen fertiliser costs while maintaining yields is estimated to deliver over $1 billion AUD of value to Australian grain growers through improved gross margins and reduced financial risk.  

As a partner, GRDC is one of the world’s leading grain research organisations. GRDC has a large existing research and development (R&D) portfolio in N and related areas, extensive research, development, and innovation networks in Australia and internationally, a strong balance sheet, and a long-term outlook. Australia is also an ideal market to incubate, develop, and scale world-leading technologies in N management given the culture of innovation, technology adoption, and adaptability in the Australian grains industry. The information below describes the opportunity for partners in more detail and the process involved.

item.title: PROC-9177462: Developing acid-soil-tolerant faba bean varieties to expand faba bean adaption.
item.description: Faba bean is an important pulse crop in Australian farming systems, providing valuable rotational benefits through biological nitrogen fixation, disease breaks and improved productivity of subsequent crops. However, production and expansion of the crop are constrained by soil acidity, particularly in Western Australia, parts of South Australia and southern New South Wales, where acidic soils reduce root growth, nodulation, nitrogen fixation and grain yield. Recent advances in genetics, genomics and phenotyping technologies provide new opportunities to accelerate the development of faba bean varieties with improved adaptation to acid soils. This investment will identify novel sources of acid soil tolerance, develop molecular markers and high throughput screening methods, and deliver breeder ready germplasm for Australian breeding programs. The goal is to improve adaptation, yield stability and productivity of faba bean in acid soil environments, supporting expansion into suitable production regions and improving the profitability and resilience of Australian farming systems. Ultimately, this investment will provide the tools and germplasm required to accelerate breeding for improved acid soil tolerance in Australian faba bean.

item.title: PROC-9177463: Enhancing faba bean seed colour and seed size uniformity to increase the value of faba beans and reduce risk of classifi
item.description: Faba bean is one of Australia’s major pulse crops and an important export commodity, with premium food markets placing strong emphasis on visual grain quality. Seed coat colour stability and seed size uniformity are key determinants of grain classification, market acceptance and price, yet deterioration in seed appearance during storage and handling can increase the risk of quality downgrades and reduce grower returns. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, digital phenotyping, genomics and molecular breeding provide new opportunities to accelerate genetic improvement of these traits. This investment will develop the knowledge, genetic resources and breeding tools required to improve seed coat colour stability and seed size uniformity in Australian faba bean, including identification of valuable genetic variation, development of high throughput phenotyping and imaging technologies, molecular marker discovery and delivery of breeder ready germplasm to Australian breeding programs. Ultimately, this investment will provide the tools and germplasm required to accelerate breeding for improved visual grain quality, helping maintain access to premium markets, reduce quality downgrades and strengthen the long-term competitiveness and value of the Australian faba bean industry.
